instagram.caption:
Plumbing and HVAC business owners: Google Local Services Ads charge for missed calls.
Google's help page, How leads work: a missed call in your business hours is charged when the caller stays on the line more than 20 seconds. Voicemail counts too.

The example: two shops, same 7 PM call.
1. Set your ad schedule to only the hours a person answers (missed calls are charged only inside both your ad schedule and your business hours).
2. Send missed rings to a second phone.
3. Text back every missed call. Follow-ups on a charged lead within 15 days are not charged again.
4. Fridays: check the Charge Status column on your Leads page.

Send this to whoever runs your Google ads.

youtube.title: Google Local Services Ads Charge for Missed Calls: The Ad Schedule Fix
youtube.description:
Google Local Services Ads missed calls: what plumbing, HVAC and electrical owners should change.
Google, "How leads work" (Local Services Help, https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435): a missed call during your business hours is charged when the customer stays on the line for more than 20 seconds; a call that goes to voicemail in your business hours is treated as connected and charged past 20 seconds; if your ad schedule differs from your business hours, missed calls are charged only inside both. Once a lead is charged, follow-up calls or messages with that customer within 15 days are not charged again.

Steps (the two shops and the hours are an example):
1. Set your ad schedule to only the hours a person answers (missed calls are charged only inside both your ad schedule and your business hours).
2. Send missed rings to a second phone.
3. Text back every missed call. Follow-ups on a charged lead within 15 days are not charged again.
4. Fridays: check the Charge Status column on your Leads page.

Send this to whoever runs your Google ads.
Next lesson: more ways to stop paying for leads you never talk to.
What a missed call costs your shop, free: https://proofnotfluff.com/missed-call-cost-calculator/
